items.title: George "Pops" Foster and Mugsy Spanier Interview, 1957-04-21
items.q: INTERVIEWER: ...And Danny Colbeck. [INTERVIEWEE] Which was always the best spot.

ctx.x: When did you make those records with Mackenzie Condon? That was a little later, huh? Uh-huh. I just made one record with Eddie and the... It was one record then? Yeah. Be some changes made, found a new baby. That's the only one I made. I didn't make sugar and all that. You mean you just made two sides? That's it? That's all. Yeah. Then later when I went to New York or I made two, I made some. The Blue Busters. And what was life like for a musician in Chicago in the 20s? Very good then. Everything. If you couldn't…

Chicago was the number one spot for musicians in the St. Louis. Chicago was St. Louis. They had both fun on in the St. Louis. But then they, and the general, they had St. Louis over. Then you go to the Beardstown, Beardstown, man. Quite a few spots. Used to take us there. Where was that? Illinois. Who had St. Louis sold up? John Rowland who? No, General Hogan as a gangster. Oh. And Danny Colbeck.
Which was always the best spot. Did you keep up your friendship with all the way through the years? Yes. I'm sorry. I'm sorry. I'm sorry. I'm sorry.
